metric.definition: Order-to-delivery time for transformers, switchgear, generators, cooling plant, and high-end accelerators.

reading.body:
Equipment lead times for data center construction, particularly transformers and switchgear, have stretched from months to years and now constrain project schedules as severely as permitting does.

This shift matters because AI scaling depends on rapid buildout of power infrastructure. When transformers take years to deliver instead of months, a data center's timeline becomes hostage to manufacturing capacity rather than construction crews or regulatory approval. The constraint is real and measurable, tracked by industry surveys that show how supply chain friction now directly limits grid expansion.

What this data does not capture is whether lead times are lengthening further, stabilizing, or improving, nor which suppliers or regions face the tightest constraints. It identifies the problem but not its trajectory. The financial impact—sunk costs from delayed projects, premium pricing for expedited orders, opportunity cost of idle facilities—sits outside this metric and would require additional reporting to quantify.
